economy._audience_comment: Growth slows as followers approach follower_soft_cap; follower_decay_per_day unfollows a share of followers every day, so audiences level off instead of growing forever. subscriber_base_churn_per_day cancels a share of subscribers daily, so they must be kept up by working.

freshness._comment: Making the same content wears it out for her audience: freshness falls by decay_per_hour while she makes it (down to floor) and recovers by recover_per_hour while she makes something else. Income and growth are multiplied by freshness.

expenses._comment: Running costs per game day, charged continuously (including while away). rent: base + per room built on a lot + the bigger-house premium. utilities: internet, power and water, base + per resident. Equipment maintenance comes from upgrades.json and room level 'upkeep_per_day'; living costs from creators.json. When cash is negative the house is behind on bills: purchases are blocked and residents get stressed (debt_mood_per_hour).

offline._comment: Time away runs the house at time_scale of the active clock (8 real hours = ~4 game days), earning at 'efficiency' while running costs are charged in full, so reopening often never beats playing.

housing._comment: max_residents caps the house regardless of bedrooms. Each extra room built costs build_cost x (1 + build_cost_growth x rooms already built).

living._comment: Each resident's living_cost_per_day (creators.json) is charged continuously, including while away, so every new housemate raises the house's running costs.

applications._comment: Before someone moves in, the house must hold a cash reserve covering reserve_days of its running costs including her own, so growth can't bankrupt the house. No money changes hands with her.

schedule._comment: Work sessions last max_minutes x lerp(min, max, work_ethic / 100), so diligent creators work longer stints.

loyalty._comment: Subscribers who dislike her current look slowly cancel: subscribers x unhappy_churn_per_hour x unhappiness, where unhappiness = sum(fan share x max(0, 1 - satisfaction)). Fan mix also drifts slowly when she isn't working.

milestones._comment: Used by the balancing simulator (tests/balance) to report progression: an established house has this many residents and net profit per day.
